THE ANNUAL COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO
THE FIFTIETH ANNUAL CONVENTION OP THE PSI UPSILON
FRATERNITY.
The Executive Council respectfully submits its Fourteenth Annual Com
munication and tenders its congratulations upon the successful accomplish
ment of another year's labor for the Fraternity.
I. Catalooue.�
In accordance with authority of the last Convention the
Treasurer has ooUected catalogue tax, amounting to $374.00. The Secretary
at once commenced , the preparation of the Beta-Beta list, which thus far con
tains 166 names. After correspondence with each member the list has been
substantiaUy completed. Circulars were prepared for getting the latest news
from 5,000 members of the Fraternity, but the Editor has thought best to
await the reduction of postage to two cents, as the work can only be properly
done in sealed correspondence, and the present rate of postage would be very
expensive. The circulars, envelopes, etc., are all ready for issue at the reduced
rate. The Editor suggests that the report of the committee appointed in 1882
on
Symbols should be received and acted upon before publication of amy sup
plementary lists of members. The present code of Symbols he regards very
unfavorably.
II. Symbols. �
The committee appointed by the last Convention to revise
and correct the Symbols of the Fraternity has made no report. Bro. R. L.
Taylor, (W '82) its chairman, lately informed the President of the last Conven
tion of his removal to Kansas and of his inability to give the matter proper
attention. The Council renews its recommendation that some adequate and
satisfactory system be devised and adopted.
III. Epitome or Convention Records. �
The preparation of this work
has been under the direction of Bro. Smiley. He has secured a fuU and com
plete set of the records, made copies of the same and epitomized about twothirds of them. The programme outlined and approved by the last Conven
tion will be carried out if no unexpected obstacles arise.
IV. Revised Constitution. �
By direction of the last General Convention
(General Eesolution No. 10, Sections II and III) the Council in June, 1882,
investigated the matter of the engrossment and lithographing of the Constitu
tion, to the end that each chapter might be provided with a correct and certi
fied copy of the instrument. The facts were submitted by letter to the various
chapters, advising them of the cost both of the Constitution alone and litho
graphed sheets, and of the cost of the Constitution in a bound blank volume
with embossed cover and Steel frontispiece and ample space for the register of
initiates for many years. Prom several of the chapters replies were
received,
but the Council learning that the committee acting under General Eesolution
No. 15, of the last ConventioB, was
